chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn 'Umar al-Yamani, who said:

God did not send a prophet at any time except that God, the Mighty and Majestic, knew that when He completed his religion, the prohibition of wine would be in it, and wine remained forbidden. Indeed, they only change the religion from one characteristic to another, and if it were a single complete matter, it would be cut off from them before the religion.
ai.seo_question: Why was the prohibition of wine not immediate in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the principle of *al-tadrij* (gradualism) in legislative revelation, illustrating how divine wisdom accommodated human nature by transitioning rulings incrementally rather than imposing them abruptly. It highlights that while the final prohibition of wine was pre-ordained, its implementation occurred through stages to ensure the community could internalize the command without rejecting the religion entirely. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of the dynamic relationship between divine decree and practical jurisprudence.
